classification.difficultyReason: The radius must be inferred from context: an inscribed circle, a semicircle on a rectangle, and two touching circles. This is harder than reading a labelled circle but needs no area calculation.

content.prompt: Identify the radius of the circular part of each shape.

answer.worked:
The circle touches opposite sides of the square, so the diameter equals the side length, $14\,\text{cm}$.
$$\begin{align*}r&=\frac{14}{2}\\r&=7\,\text{cm}\end{align*}$$

The semicircle sits across the full width of the rectangle, so the diameter is $1.8\,\text{m}$.
$$\begin{align*}r&=\frac{1.8}{2}\\r&=0.9\,\text{m}\end{align*}$$

The two touching circles together span two diameters.
$$\begin{align*}d&=\frac{20}{2}\\d&=10\,\text{cm}\\r&=\frac{10}{2}\\r&=5\,\text{cm}\end{align*}$$
